chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Khalid ibn 'Umara, from Abu Baseer, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When the barrier is placed between him and speech, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) comes to him, and whomever Allah wills. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) sits on his right, and the other one on his left. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) says to him: 'As for what you hoped for, it is before you, and as for what you feared from it, you have been made safe from it.'

Then a door to Paradise is opened for him, and they say: 'This is your dwelling place in Paradise. If you wish, we can return you to the world, and for you there will be gold and silver therein.' He says: 'I have no need of the world.' At that, his color whitens, his forehead sweats, his lips contract, his nostrils spread, and his left eye sheds tears. Whichever of these signs you see, suffice with it.

When the soul exits the body, it is presented to it just as it was presented to him while in the body, and it chooses the Hereafter. He is washed among those who wash him, and turned over among those who turn him over. When he is enshrouded in his kafans and placed on his bed, his soul comes out walking in front of the people. The souls of the believers meet him, greet him, and give him glad tidings of what Allah, Exalted is His Praise, has prepared for him from the bounties.

When he is placed in his grave, the soul is returned to him up to his hips. Then he is asked about what he knows. When he provides what he knows, that door which the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) showed him is opened for him, and its light, brightness, coolness, and fragrant breeze enter upon him.

He said: I said, 'May I be your ransom, where is the squeezing of the grave?' He said: 'Far be it! There is no squeezing upon the believers from it. By Allah, this earth (of the believer) boasts over that earth (of the disbeliever), saying: 'A believer trod upon my back, and a believer did not tread upon you.' And the earth says to it: 'By Allah, I used to love you when you were walking upon my back. But when I am made to love you, you shall soon know what I will do with you.' So it expands for him to the extent of his vision.
ai.seo_question: What happens to a believer's soul and grave after death according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi elaborates on the eschatological comfort of the believer, highlighting the unique Shia emphasis on the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) personal presence during the transition of death. It details the soul's voluntary rejection of worldly wealth in favor of Paradise, followed by the specific signs of a good death and the absence of grave constriction (dagh-t), illustrating the believer's elevated status in the intermediate realm (Barzakh).
